subject: Case FaxRxTx / Venali · worldwide fax platform, 2007–2009 · outcome known · test build of the generic report assembler
standfirst: The validation case — the only one this project has with a documented outcome. The chain was run end to end and the number written down and closed before the outcome was opened. A reference-class reading was taken separately, in ignorance of the chain, and lands on the other side of the outcome. This build reproduces the report of 2026-08-26 through the generic assembler; no figure is new.

sections.title: How to read the chart
sections.lead: Both instruments produce a distribution. Only one of them did so without being asked.
sections.html:
Both instruments produce a distribution. The outside view produces quantiles natively; the bottom-up's range comes from the optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic value in every rate cell, summed under a declared item correlation of ρ = 0.5 — independent items would claim the total is known to about ±2%, perfectly correlated ones would give about ×1.9, and the truth is certainly neither. Across ρ from 0.25 to 0.75 the band edges move about ±20%. The width of the red bell is therefore a property of the rate table and of that convention, not of the project; what each curve's width does and does not contain is tabulated in docs/sensors/README.md.

Curves that must not be read as one

Each curve answers a different question. The outside view says where projects of this class landed against their early estimates — that width is the class's heterogeneity, the risk of the project. The bottom-up says what this work costs at the pinned rates — its width is the rates' spread under the declared correlation. A no-method family says what a bare model guesses on the same text, one thin curve per run, never pooled — its spread is the model's, not the project's. A parametric curve prices the functional shell only. Two readings of the outside view are one sensor run twice on the same input; where they disagree, the distance between them is that sensor's own uncertainty about the level, and neither is averaged with the other. Only the marked quantiles are readings; the curve between them is interpolation.

The unit, and the one conversion applied

Net hours of work on the task, shown as person-days of 8 such hours. Leave, public holidays and sickness are not in these numbers, and neither is any notion of calendar or headcount. Every sensor declares its own unit before its figures; the class readings are converted to task hours by the factor their own declarations contain, applied to the class side only — the bottom-up needs none, having been priced in task hours to begin with. The comparison-layer conversion to staffed person-months is the author's constant (docs/constants.md §4a) and appears in the text, never on the chart.

Known direction of error

The bottom-up curve is a normal approximation. Rate cells are right-skewed and correlated sums keep skew, so the true upper tail is fatter than drawn.

sections.title: Against the outcome
sections.lead: This is the only case in the project with a documented outcome, and the only place any of the method's claims can be scored at all.
sections.html:
gate
The chain lands inside the ×1.3 gate ×1.17
11 386 net task hours against an outcome of about 13 304 (120 staffed person-months at the case's own conversion, run 33). The number was written down and closed before the outcome was opened (run 32).
corridor
The outcome sits at about P85 of the declared corridor
The corridor is the rate table's O/M/P spread under ρ = 0.5, a convention; that the outcome falls inside it at P85 is one observation, not a calibration.
class
The outside view lands on the other side ×1.17 high
The class median, 140 person-months in the unit the outcome is recorded in, is ×1.17 above the outcome where the chain is ×0.86 below it. Neither is averaged.

sections.title: Findings
sections.lead: Produced without being asked for, by instruments whose job was something else.
sections.html:
sizing
Four elements refused as unsizeable by both repeats
A schema that names a platform and not an entity kind, a handler defined by a question, an integration interface with neither direction nor payload, a scope baseline that names no function. Named holes, never guessed (run 31).
parametric
Function points price the shell ×22 low · by design
23–27 of 52 obligations sit outside what function points count — telephony, routing, rendering, the points of presence. The parametric instrument's place on this chart is the measure of that.

sections.title: Defaults
sections.lead: Each is a fork the document leaves open and the estimate had to close. The reading taken is inside the centre; the reading refused is not. One row per entry of the assumption log, its first paragraph.
sections.html:
A1
Estimation scope
The full cycle for the "the team did" list from SYSTEM.md §6: the phase of domain immersion and architecture/technology selection (~1–2 months) + design + development + testing + rollout to production of the new version of the core functionality replacing the first version. - Included: rendering and OCR workers, the cluster with the delivery-control mechanism (watchdogs + tokens), NOC, the user portal, the inbound-email parser, saving CDR/billing data, integration tests on the real stream with comparison to the old system. - Not included: the PoP software, the routing program, billing,…
A2
Definition of Done
The new system takes production traffic in prod; the integration tests on the real stream have passed, the results agree with the old system; the old version can be decommissioned.
A3
Team and starting conditions
The team did not know the domain — immersion in the subject area, discussions, and technology selection took ~1–2 months (included in A1). Mitigating factor: a working v1 exists as a live reference of requirements ("like v1, but fix what we don't like") — there is no full-scale requirements gathering from scratch, but the domain (fax protocols, telecom, distributed delivery) is new to the team. Blended composition, including QA and PM. The team's headcount is not part of the assumptions (the volume of work is estimated, not the calendar).
A4
Reuse
No first-version code in the new one ("no reference base classes"). Reused: the ready PoP software, the ready routing, a third-party OCR library, rendering via a printer driver (Black Ice-class), the existing storage infrastructure (Lustre) and the DB as technologies — we do not develop these, only integrate with them.
A5
Technological era
2007–2009: C#/.NET ~3.x, a Windows cluster on our own hardware, no clouds and no ready orchestrators (what a message broker/Kubernetes would give today is written by hand — watchdogs, tokens, delivery control). MSMQ deliberately excluded from the negative experience of v1.
A6
Target scale
The engineering target — ~1 million faxes / 10-hour day (~30/s on average), with bursts up to ~10× (~300/s, "10 million/day" — an estimate of the peak mode). A cluster of ~16–20 nodes, 10–20 PoPs. The estimate is made for designing to the nominal with burst resilience: distribution, surviving failures, and delivery control of every fax are mandatory properties, not options.
A7
Rendering formats
8–10 input formats (DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF, TXT, GIF, TIFF + possibly 1–3 forgotten ones). Each format is a separate piece of integration and stabilization work, not a "free" extension of the list.
A8
Organizational context
A product company (Venali), an internal rework by management decision. There is no hard deadline, but there is pressure. The process — a planning phase, then scrum. Approvals are internal, faster than the enterprise client of the BMS example. Accounted for in reference class (decomposition, by construction, does not see it).
A9
Units
Estimation in person-months (1 pm ≈ 21 pd ≈ 168 hours), the total effort of the whole team, including QA/PM and the architecture-selection phase. Conversion to a calendar duration is a separate step, not part of the runs.

sections.title: Estimate gaps
sections.lead: Not oversights. Each is a thing the chain refused to price, with the reason it refused.
sections.html:
1
Seven named holes
Items the sizing sensors refused to size, listed by the assembly and priced at nothing.
2
No calibration Steps B–D not run
The centre is the table-priced assembly as it stands; the gap-blind rate round and the diagnosis were not run on this case in this generation.
3
The rate table's level
Uncalibrated against any outcome; this case is the one place it has been scored, once.

sections.title: Where every number came from
sections.lead: Each sensor is an engine with a version, stamped on its own output. They are hired for what they are forbidden to see, not for autonomy.
sections.html:
1
Product model · n = 2 · Hotyn-M 1.1
47 product obligations → 97 elements; the second reading differs ×1.02 in structure. Produces no effort figure of any kind.
2
Work model · Hotyn-W 1.1
Crossed against the declared technology in three batches → 570 work items on 96 elements. Work the product needs but no declared activity covers is reported as a finding, never invented.
3
Size classes · n = 2 · Hotyn-D 2.0
Each element classified by counting named things, the enumeration being the justification. Class agreement 87.3%; whole-chain repeat spread ×1.033.
4
Rate table uncalibrated
External norms in net task hours, gap-blind: never saw a project total, a budget, or a gap a rate would explain.
5
Outside view · Lytin-R 1.1
Ran in ignorance of all of the above, the unit convention withheld so that it declared its own: funded seats × time, all roles — the same unit the outcome is recorded in.
P
Parametric · Hotyn-P 1.0 / Hotyn-N 1.0
Function points counted from the pinned obligation list by a sensor that never sees weights or effort, priced on two published effort curves. The functional shell only.
F
The outcome
Sealed before the estimate, opened after the number was written down and closed (run 32).

Two coordinates, not one

An estimate is a property of the triple (project × engine × model). Every sensor on this case ran on Claude Opus 5, so the model coordinate is held fixed and the readings are engine-and-project readings only.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.lead: This report is one output of a method that is written down. Nothing below is specific to this case; every file states what it is for, what it may not do, and what would change it.
sections.html:
frame
METHODOLOGY.md
Why independence of techniques replaces independence of experts, what each method is structurally blind to, and why a divergence is diagnosed rather than averaged.
chain
docs/instrument.md
What actually runs: the product model, the crossing against a declared technology, the size classes, the pinned table, the script. What is pinned at each step and what each sensor is forbidden to produce.
curves
docs/sensors/
One note per curve on this chart: what the sensor was conceived as, what question it answers, what its width includes and leaves out, what has been measured about it, how to read its output, what may change.
numbers
docs/constants.md
Every constant the method has, and the comparison-layer conversion pinned by the author: 6 net task hours per present day, ×1.10 leave, 21 days — so 1 staffed person-month ≈ 114.5 net task hours.
case
docs/case_profile.md
Team grade, site count, domain familiarity and the outcome's unit are pinned before any estimate exists, so that no condition can be chosen after a number is on the table.
isolation
PIPELINE.md
The visibility matrix: who may see what, in what order the sensors are launched, and the disciplines that are mechanically checkable rather than promised.
prices
docs/rate_table.md · technology_catalogue.md
The pinned rates, in net person-hours, written gap-blind by a role that never saw a project total. And the vocabulary a technology declaration is written in.
done
docs/exit_criterion.md
When the instrument may be called fit for use, decided in advance: repeatability, position against human estimators, calibratability against outcomes.
this case
this case's folder
The pinned inputs, the case profile, the assumption log, the technology declaration, and every run with its raw sensor output kept verbatim.

fine: What this report is not. Not a validated price, and not a price at all — it is work content in net task hours, shown as person-days of 8 such hours. Converting it into money, calendar or headcount is the reader's act, using the reader's own figures. Every bottom-up number rests on a rate table of external industry norms calibrated against no outcome.

What it is. The estimate, its corridor, the disagreement between two structurally independent methods stated rather than averaged away, and, on the record, the obligations, the findings, the questions and the defaults that the number is standing on.
